extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians/authors preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Pacific Journal of Mathematics (PJM)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Pacific Journal of Mathematics, covering ethical requirements, formatting, required items (abstract, MSC, references, figures), and post-acceptance steps (source files, proofs, arXiv DOI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to meet our ethical guidelines on intellectual property, plagiarism, contributorship, and disclosure of financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the full policies for authors (linked). Authors must follow the journal's policies on IP, plagiarism, contributorship, and disclosure of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript acknowledges that the manuscript is original and is not, in whole or in part, published or under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must attest the manuscript will not be submitted elsewhere while under consideration by PJM. The submitted article must not be a revision of a rejected article previously submitted to this journal, unless the authors have been explicitly invited to resubmit by the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use AI tools for light editing, such as spell-checking and help with grammar, without acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any use of AI in aid of the arguments in a paper or the citations in a paper must be acknowledged. Papers largely created by AI may not be submitted to this journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of editor
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, authors will be asked to suggest one or more suitable editors to initially handle their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the editor whose interests are closest to the subject of the paper, but who is not directly connected to one of the authors (e.g., former advisor/student, close relative, colleague at the same institution, or close collaborator). Manuscripts may be reassigned to another editor after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be in English, French or German.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required format: PDF from amsart LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requires uploading the submission in PDF. The pdf must be printed from a LaTeX source file in which the command \documentclass[12pt]{amsart} is active, at the start of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No changes which affect horizontal or vertical margins, or line spacing, should be made. While the system will accept submission of a pdf which violates this rule, you may be required by PJM editorial management to resubmit a version in the correct format. If your submission is accepted, you will need to supply the LaTeX source file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line numbers (suggested)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly suggested that you add the command \usepackage[pagewise]{lineno}\linenumbers to the preamble since the addition of line numbers can save the referee substantial tedious effort and hence facilitates obtaining referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not add line numbers, you may be asked to do so later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of about 150 words or less in English must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should be self-contained and not make any reference to the bibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords and subject codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords and at least one Mathematics Subject Classification code for the article are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each coauthor, postal address and affiliation (if appropriate) are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each coauthor must provide a valid email address that belongs only to that person and is not shared with anyone. Changes in email address should be communicated promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: References
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical references should be complete, including article titles and page ranges. All references in the bibliography should be cited in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of BibTeX is preferred but not required. Tags will be converted to the journal format. Authors attest that all documents listed in the bibliography have been read and absorbed by at least one author; their relevance to the submission should be highlighted by a description explicit enough to orient the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be of publication quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance, submit the original source files in vector graphics format for all diagrams (vector EPS or vector PDF preferred). Bundle figure files into a single archive (zip, tar, rar, etc.) and upload at acceptance time. For questions, email graphics@msp.org. Each figure should be captioned and numbered so that it can float. Small figures can be kept in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints / arXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: If your paper has previously been deposited on arXiv, we will need its arXiv number at acceptance time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows PJM to deposit the DOI of the published version on the paper’s arXiv page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Page proofs will be made available to authors (or to the designated corresponding author) in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to acknowledge the receipt of proofs or to return corrections within the requested deadline may cause publication to be postponed.
